body:
### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.clue

### Question

Can `timeoutlen` be respected for leader key to be mapped to something past timeout? Currently, mini.clue seems to prevent `timeoutlen` (as intended because it has to show the menu), displaying menu and waiting for next key indefinitely. I'd like to bind leader key to e.g. `ciw` in normal mode if it is pressed and no other keys are pressed during timeout. Ideally, respect `timeoutlen` for top level leader key binding e.g. `<space>a` (I don't really want a menu for these keys anyway since they tend to be easier to remember), but subsequent layers maintain current behavior showing menu and not timing out.

Any ideas or is it assumed all mini.clue users don't care for `timeoutlen`?

-------

Completely unrelated, but I'm also thinking of binding repeats for ftFT to ftFT and freeing up convenient keybindings to `,` and `;`. Curious if there are any reasons this might be a bad idea other than it's not the default binding. Is this easy to achieve with native Neovim functions without a dedicated plugin? `,` and `;` can be another leader key or some other useful mapping.

Thanks.

comment_data.body:
> Can `timeoutlen` be respected for leader key to be mapped to something past timeout? Currently, mini.clue seems to prevent `timeoutlen` (as intended because it has to show the menu), displaying menu and waiting for next key indefinitely.

Yes, this is an intended and [documented](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-clue.html#miniclue-key-query-process) behavior. 

> Any ideas or is it assumed all mini.clue users don't care for `timeoutlen`?

It is the core idea behind triggers in 'mini.clue' to be independent of 'timeoutlen' so that there is no "pressure" to execute a potentially new mapping sequence and be able to see the possible choices.

> I'd like to bind leader key to e.g. `ciw` in normal mode if it is pressed and no other keys are pressed during timeout.

My genuine suggestion is to not do that and either find another key for that or getting into habit of doing `ciw` explicitly (which is what I recommend and what feels like a better long term choice).

---

> Completely unrelated, but I'm also thinking of binding repeats for ftFT to ftFT and freeing up convenient keybindings to `,` and `;`.

This is the behavior of ['mini.jump'](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/readmes/mini-jump.html). It can be configured to not map `;` key for repeat.
